vocabTest.title: Free English vocabulary test
vocabTest.metaTitle: Free English vocabulary test: how many words do you know?
vocabTest.metaDescription: Take the free 2-minute English vocabulary test and see your full results without an account. Save your result and get a PDF with a free account.
vocabTest.introLead: Find out how many English words you know and get book recommendations for your level.
vocabTest.introFacts: Free · No account needed · First result after 8 questions
vocabTest.intro: You see one English word at a time with three meanings and “None of these”. Pick the right one, or tap “Not sure” if you do not know the word: guessing makes the result less accurate. After each answer you see whether it was right, and the next word appears by itself. The first three words are of medium difficulty. After that, words are sampled around your estimated level. After 8 words you can see your result; the more you answer, the narrower the range. The test covers words up to the 40,000 most common. We do not store your answers on our server. Your last result stays in this browser for 30 days. This browser also remembers which words you were asked, so your next test uses new words.
vocabTest.explain: This is an estimate. It counts word families, such as "help", "helps" and "helped" as one word.

faq.title: Questions about the test
faq.howQ: How does the vocabulary test work?
faq.howA: You see one English word at a time and pick its meaning from three options or “None of these”. The first three words are of medium difficulty. After that, words are sampled around your estimated level. You can see your result after 8 words.
faq.accuracyA: The result is a range, not a single number. The more words you answer, the narrower the range. Word families count as one word, so “help”, “helps” and “helped” are one word. Choosing “Not sure” instead of guessing keeps the result accurate.
faq.freeQ: Is the test free? Do I need an account?
faq.freeA: You can take the free test and see your full results without an account. A free Readfox account is needed only to save your result and receive it by email as a PDF.
faq.levelQ: What does my level mean for reading?
faq.levelA: Your vocabulary size maps to a CEFR level from A1 to C2. The test suggests free books where you already know about 95% of the words, which is the point where reading becomes comfortable.
